note: Independent rejudgment at HEAD ecb3e9830f after f13306e437 (owner ruling 2026-10-24, "No follow the RFC") dropped the {partial} deviation. draft-ietf-bess-mup-safi Section 3.1.3.1 (rfc/drafts/draft-ietf-bess-mup-safi.txt): "The Source Address Length has a fixed length of 1 octet." and "compute the number of remaining octets by subtracting, from the Length field in the MUP NLRI common header, the offset of the end of the Source Address measured from the start of the Route Type specific field", then "- < 0:   the mandatory fields exceed the declared Length; the NLRI is malformed; MUST be treated as Treat-as-withdraw." Producer at HEAD: internal/component/bgp/plugins/nlri/mup/types.go::parseBodyT1ST returns ErrMUPTruncated for a Length ending inside the prefix (parsePrefixField), inside TEID/QFI/Endpoint Address Length (len(rest) < fixedLen), inside the Endpoint Address, at the end of the Endpoint Address with no Source Address Length octet (len(rest) == 0, the draft-mpmz-bess-mup-safi-02 form, which no longer reads as length 0), and inside a non-zero Source Address. Letter and spirit: the code now complies on every shape; the -02 deviation is gone, sourceOctetAbsent and the relay canonicalisation deleted, so a missing mandatory field is no longer supplied by assumption. The tests, four questions. (1) What the draft says: TestMUPT1STMandatoryFieldsWithinLength (nlri/mup/draft_ietf_bess_mup_safi_tlv_mup_test.go) asserts ErrorIs ErrMUPTruncated for t1stBody cut inside the endpoint (2 of 4 octets) and, new, for t1stThroughEndpoint (ends at the endpoint, no Source Address Length), positive NoError, empty rest, exact TEID 0x3039 and endpoint 10.0.0.1. TestMUPMalformedT1STTreatAsWithdraw (reactor/draft_ietf_bess_mup_safi_t1st_withdraw_test.go) holds K0, receives the same key with its endpoint cut by 2 octets between siblings L and L2 (L2 with unknown TLV 0xF0), and asserts ActionNone, MP_REACH exactly L||L2, MP_UNREACH exactly K0 and decodable; negative asserts a well-formed UPDATE comes back byte-identical. That is RFC 7606 Section 2 treat-as-withdraw, not merely what the code does. (2) For the two boundaries tagged, yes: restoring the lenient len(rest)==0 return nil fails the -02 ErrorIs; dropping the endpoint check either returns a short endpoint (ErrorIs fails) or panics. The recorded discrimination is only a revert-to-panic of parseBodyT1ST and ValidateNLRI, which proves the units reach the producers, not these branches; this answer rests on reading. (3) Isolated: TEID nonzero, Endpoint Address Length 32 valid, siblings well formed; only the truncation fires. (4) Whole requirement: no, and this is the finding. The rule measures to the end of the Source Address, and no tagged unit feeds a route whose Length ends inside a non-zero Source Address, inside the 6 fixed octets, or inside the prefix. ParseMUP slices body with two indices (types.go, data[mupHeaderLen : mupHeaderLen+bodyLen]), so its capacity runs into the next NLRI: deleting parseBodyT1ST's len(rest) < sourceOctets check reads the source address out of the following NLRI's octets and then panics on rest[sourceOctets:], and deleting the fixedLen check panics on rest[4]; every tagged unit stays green under both mutants, so the tags cannot fail on that non-compliance. Untagged corroboration, no credit: reactor/t1st_02_relay_test.go TestMUPT1ST02TreatAsWithdraw proves the -02 route leaves MP_REACH and is withdrawn by K0's bytes at the session; nlri/mup/json_test.go covers an ISD prefix shorter than its length through the shared parsePrefixField. Owed to reach enforced: a tagged negative for a T1ST whose Length ends inside a non-zero (32-bit) Source Address and one ending inside TEID/QFI/Endpoint Address Length, each asserting ErrorIs ErrMUPTruncated; optionally tag TestMUPT1ST02TreatAsWithdraw. Implemented and tested at the endpoint and -02 boundaries; implemented but unverified at the source-address, fixed-field and prefix boundaries.
